Regulatory Transformation

Regulatory Transformation: navigating emerging risks, driving AI adoption and reducing regulatory burden

Regulators are facing a shifting operating environment as technology, markets, environmental pressures and societal expectations evolve faster than traditional regulatory frameworks. Fragmented data and limited intelligence continue to make risk prioritisation difficult.

There is a growing opportunity to use advanced analytics to better target regulatory effort. Many regulators are still working to integrate data across systems, uplift analytical capability and embed insights into everyday decision-making.

AI adoption is also becoming a core regulatory transformation issue. Regulators are seeking to balance opportunities for automation and improved risk identification with the need to manage governance, transparency, bias, legal risk, privacy and public confidence.

At the same time, governments are under pressure to reduce red tape, make faster decisions and manage fiscal constraints. This is driving interest in regulatory consolidation, shared-service models and more consistent approaches to regulatory delivery, while maintaining fairness and strong outcomes.

Regulation Hub Intelligence Brief

AI Brief 125 articles across 8 categories

The fortnight is shaped by three converging regulator investment themes: enforcement escalation across ASIC, TEQSA, AUSTRAC, and ACQSC converting supervisory intent into active action; AI governance acceleration driven by a Commonwealth health-system breach, the AEC inquiry, ABA submission, and ASQA principles creating a cross-sector AI risk mandate; and structural reform execution with the Financial Advice Reform Bill, NDIS sustainability redesign, defence procurement reset, and AUKUS leasing alternatives all shifting from policy to implementation. ASIC's 2026–27 supervisory priorities and life insurance sector paper name specific product governance and sustainable finance disclosure obligations that will drive near-term compliance uplift demand across banks, platforms, and insurers. APRA's simultaneous private credit risk warning and proposed reforms expected to land hardest on platform operators create a two-front assurance and risk advisory mandate for mid-tier ADIs and superannuation trustees — the target list is now named. The ATSB's Port Botany findings and AMSA's emissions reduction plan signal transport regulators converting investigation outcomes into enforceable standards, opening the SMS uplift and maritime compliance readiness window before deadlines crystallise. TEQSA's updated Compliance and Enforcement Policy paired with active enforcement against OneGlobe and Opulence marks a structural shift in higher education regulatory risk that peers of those providers must now address. KPMG should concentrate BD effort this fortnight on financial services platform operators, rail and maritime clients, mid-tier higher education providers, and Commonwealth health and defence clients — all facing live compliance deadlines or active regulatory scrutiny.

Cross-category themes

Regulators across virtually every sector are simultaneously escalating enforcement posture and advancing structural reform, creating a dual pressure of immediate compliance obligations and forward-looking legislative redesign that demands both gap-assessment and policy-shaping advisory responses. Cross-cutting themes include heightened transparency and governance disclosure requirements (spanning financial services, education, defence, and energy), coordinated child and consumer safety enforcement across multiple agencies, and the embedding of AI and emerging technology governance into sector-specific compliance frameworks, each representing a live advisory opportunity for KPMG's regulatory practice.

Separately, lodge a KPMG submission to the Home Affairs Horizon 2 consultation before it closes to build direct relationship capital with the department and position KPMG's cyber advisory bench for the delivery wave that follows strategy finalisation.

Brief the health regulatory and financial crime partners this fortnight on Ahpra's psychology reform implementation transition and AUSTRAC's SMR capability push — both clients are past policy design and at the delivery-contracting window where KPMG's workforce and regulatory program design offering converts. Brief ASIC-regulated financial services and life insurance partners this fortnight on the 2026–27 supervisory priorities, and use AUSTRAC's infringement notice campaign as the trigger to convert existing AML/CTF relationships into structured compliance assurance mandates before the enforcement sweep widens to the broader enrolled register.

  • Tech & AI: Brief the Home Affairs and NDIS Commission partners this fortnight on a joint Horizon 2 cyber strategy and AI governance engagement — the consultation deadline and the NDIS portal go-live together create a single accelerated entry point before machinery-of-government decisions lock the vendor landscape for 18 months.
  • Capability reviews: Brief the Health and Human Services sector partner this fortnight on a joint pursuit targeting Ahpra and the NDIS Commission — Ahpra's psychology reform next phase and the Commission's complaint backlog together constitute a pipeline of regulatory capability and operating model work that will be awarded before calendar year-end.
  • Learning & development: Brief the health regulatory and financial crime partners this fortnight on Ahpra's psychology reform implementation transition and AUSTRAC's SMR capability push — both clients are past policy design and at the delivery-contracting window where KPMG's workforce and regulatory program design offering converts.
  • Risk & assurance: Brief ASIC-regulated financial services and life insurance partners this fortnight on the 2026–27 supervisory priorities, and use AUSTRAC's infringement notice campaign as the trigger to convert existing AML/CTF relationships into structured compliance assurance mandates before the enforcement sweep widens to the broader enrolled register.

State-gov priorities

Cited strategic priorities across all 9 jurisdictions, refreshed bi-annually. Every source URL is .gov.au.

Housing supply is the most consistent cross-jurisdictional priority, with ACT, NSW, QLD, TAS, VIC, and WA all carrying explicit dwelling targets ranging from 10,000 affordable homes in Tasmania to 2.24 million homes in Victoria's 2051 plan — creating sustained demand for planning reform implementation, delivery assurance, and housing finance advisory. A parallel infrastructure wave underpins these targets, with every jurisdiction holding a multi-billion, multi-year capital program and several (SA, WA, ACT) anchored to formal 20-year infrastructure strategies that cycle through periodic updates and government response processes. Renewable energy and net-zero transition is near-universal in intent but diverges sharply in ambition and framing: SA and TAS are pursuing genuine generation leadership (100% renewables by 2027 and 200% by 2040 respectively), while NT and QLD continue to centre resources, mining, and agriculture as the primary economic engine, with the Commonwealth's Future Made in Australia attempting to bridge both camps through critical minerals and clean-energy manufacturing. Defence industry emerges as a distinct sub-theme across the Commonwealth ($330B IIP), WA (Defence West 2025–2040), and NSW (sovereign manufacturing), forming a loosely connected industrial strategy corridor where capability uplift, supply chain assurance, and workforce planning are under-served. Law and order is an outlier cluster concentrated in NT and QLD, where crime reduction and youth justice reform signal a harder-right policy turn that contrasts with VIC's Royal Commission mental health investment and ACT's wellbeing-budgeting approach, pointing to genuine divergence in community safety philosophy rather than shared direction. Health system capacity — safe staffing in NSW, aged care transition nationally, Tasmania's 2040 plan, and VIC's mental health capital program — represents a slow-moving but high-value reform agenda where workforce modelling, program assurance, and change management are consistent gaps. For KPMG, the strongest immediate BD surface is housing delivery assurance and planning reform implementation across NSW, VIC, QLD, and ACT, where political pressure to hit headline targets is outpacing jurisdictional delivery capacity; the second is the Commonwealth–state interface on Future Made in Australia, Defence, and hydrogen, where stakeholder consultation and investment facilitation mandates are still being defined.

Last refreshed 2026-07-01. Bi-annual schedule; source URLs verified to .gov.au.

Commonwealth

  • Future Made in Australia
    The Treasury / Department of Industry, Science and Resources 2024-2034 (10-year, $22.7B package)
    Program design, sector assessment frameworks, investment mandate design, industry consultation, economic modelling, community benefit evaluation
    Source (2024-05-14)
  • Strengthening Medicare
    Department of Health, Disability and Ageing 2023-2027 (reform rolling); Budget 2025-26 expansion from Nov 2025
    Primary care reform evaluation, Urgent Care Clinic rollout support, workforce modelling, digital health implementation, Medicare integrity assurance
    Source (2024-05-14)
  • 2024 National Defence Strategy and Integrated Investment Program
    Department of Defence 2024-2034 ($330B Integrated Investment Program to 2033-34)
    Capability program assurance, workforce strategy, sovereign industrial capability priorities, AUKUS implementation support, capability reviews
    Source (2024-04-17)
  • APS Reform Agenda
    Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet / Australian Public Service Commission 2022-ongoing (4 pillars, 59 initiatives; Public Service Amendment Act 2024 enacted)
    Integrity and capability reviews, workforce strategy, stewardship framework design, data & digital workforce planning, contractor-to-APS conversion support
    Source (2024-12-01)
  • Working for Women: A Strategy for Gender Equality
    Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (Office for Women) 2024-2034 (10-year strategy)
    Gender impact analysis, workplace gender equality evaluation, Government Board appointment strategy support, pay-gap economic modelling, consultation design
    Source (2024-03-07)
  • Aged Care reform – transition to Support at Home
    Department of Health, Disability and Ageing Aged Care Act 2024 commenced 1 Nov 2025; CHSP transition to Support at Home by 1 Jul 2027
    Provider transition support, data and digital strategy implementation, workforce modelling, single assessment system evaluation, consumer journey design
    Source (2024-07-01)

New South Wales

  • Safe Staffing Levels in NSW public hospitals
    NSW Ministry of Health Phase one early 2024; full rollout 2,480 FTE nurses/midwives by June 2027
    Workforce modelling, implementation assurance, change management support, clinical governance advisory, rostering system review
    Source (2024-03-11)
  • Transport Oriented Development Program (TOD)
    Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure TOD planning controls commenced 13 May 2024; 15-year horizon; 170,000+ homes
    Precinct planning, inclusionary zoning advisory, infrastructure funding strategy, development feasibility, stakeholder consultation
    Source (2024-05-13)
  • Sydney Metro – Western Sydney Airport and Sydney Metro West
    Transport for NSW / Sydney Metro Western Sydney Airport line opens 2026; Metro West completion by 2032; network to 46 stations by 2030
    Program assurance, capability reviews, cost estimation reviews, land use integration, precinct economic analysis
    Source (2024-06-01)
  • Bringing back manufacturing to NSW (state-owned energy and rollingstock)
    Cabinet Office / Treasury NSW / Transport for NSW 2023-2027+ (current Parliament)
    Industrial strategy advisory, local content analysis, state-owned corporation establishment, procurement strategy, workforce development
    Source (2024-09-01)
  • NSW Budget 2025-26 priorities (essential services + diversified economy)
    NSW Treasury 2025-26 forward estimates to 2028-29
    Fiscal strategy advisory, expenditure review, program evaluation, revenue analysis, investment prioritisation
    Source (2025-06-24)
  • Safer Pathway – domestic and family violence response
    Department of Communities and Justice Statewide rollout ongoing; DFV reforms 2024-ongoing
    Service design, outcomes evaluation, risk assessment framework review, cross-agency data sharing advisory, program logic review
    Source (2024-01-01)

Victoria

  • Victoria's Housing Statement – The Decade Ahead 2024-2034
    Department of Transport and Planning 2024-2034 (800,000 homes / 80,000 per year target)
    Planning reform advisory, activity centre masterplans, affordable housing economics, surplus land unlocking, stakeholder consultation, LGA target negotiations
    Source (2023-09-20)
  • Plan for Victoria (long-term plan to 2051)
    Department of Transport and Planning Released Feb 2025; horizon to 2051 (2.24 million homes target)
    LGA housing target analysis, settlement pattern modelling, sustainability and climate policy integration, First Peoples self-determination in planning, infrastructure sequencing
    Source (2025-02-01)
  • Mental Health and Wellbeing reform (Royal Commission implementation)
    Department of Health 2021-2031 (decade of reform); Statewide Service and Capital Plan 2024-2037
    Service design, capital planning, workforce strategy, outcomes evaluation, lived experience engagement design, Mental Health Levy economic analysis
    Source (2024-07-01)
  • Treaty for Victoria / First Peoples' self-determination
    First Peoples – State Relations Statewide Treaty Bill 2025 introduced; negotiations ongoing
    Closing the Gap accountability framework design, service commissioning transition, policy impact analysis, governance advisory for new representative body
    Source (2025-02-01)
  • Breakthrough Victoria Fund – research and innovation commercialisation
    Department of Jobs, Skills, Industry and Regions 2020-2030 ($2B 10-year fund; $1.3B co-investment leveraged by 2024)
    Commercialisation strategy, innovation ecosystem review, investment thesis advisory, co-investment deal structuring, industry sector analysis
    Source (2024-06-30)
